title: Transfer: clean the station log

creation.briefMd: Step one of the log scrubber. Nobody at the field station writes the log the same way twice: stray spaces, shouted levels, blank lines, and notes to self starting with a hash. This step builds the normaliser — one function that turns a messy line into the one canonical form, and one that runs it over a whole log and drops what is not a record. The next step in the creation gives it a real file to read and a report to write.

blocks.md:
## One canonical shape, chosen up front

Cleaning text is not a pile of tweaks; it is a decision about what the tidy version looks like, followed by the steps that get there. Decide the shape first — what is trimmed, what case each field is in, what counts as a record at all — and every line either reaches that shape or is dropped.

This bites when the steps run in an order that undoes each other. Collapsing internal whitespace before trimming the ends leaves a leading space behind; lowercasing the whole line first destroys a field you wanted upper case. The order is part of the rule, not an implementation detail.

```python
import re

messy = "   fox   Seen  NEAR  the  creek "

tidy = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", messy.strip())
print(repr(tidy))         # 'fox Seen NEAR the creek'
print(tidy.split(" ", 1)) # ['fox', 'Seen NEAR the creek'] - one split, two parts

print(bool("# note".startswith("#")))   # True - not a record
```

A common mistake is assuming every line has the fields you expect and letting `split` unpack straight into three names, which raises `ValueError` on the first short line. The exercise asks you to normalise real station log lines: trim, collapse runs of spaces, shout the level, quieten the message, and drop blanks, comments, and anything too short to be a record.

blocks.promptMd: You collapse runs of whitespace before trimming the ends. What does `"  fox   seen  "` become?

choices.md: `' fox seen '` — the outer spaces each collapsed to one and stayed

blocks.explainMd: Collapsing turns each run into a single space, including the runs at the two ends, so a lone space survives on each side. Trimming first removes the ends entirely and then the collapse only has internal runs left to deal with — same two steps, different result.

blocks.promptMd: Which lines should a log normaliser drop rather than clean?

choices.md: Blank lines, comment lines, and lines with too few fields to be a record
Any line that is already upper case
Any line longer than eighty characters

blocks.explainMd: A normaliser has two answers: here is the canonical form, or this was never a record. Blanks and comments are the obvious second case, and so is a line too short to have the fields the shape requires — cleaning that one would invent data that was not there.

blocks.promptMd: > Write `clean_line(line)` returning `"<stamp> <LEVEL> <rest in lower case>"` or `None` for a blank line, a `#` comment, or a line with fewer than three fields. Then write `clean_log(lines)` returning only the cleaned records.

checks.equals: ['2041-03-02 ERR north sensor cold', '2041-03-02 WARN east damp']

hintLadder.md: The starter returns every line exactly as it came in, comments and blanks included, so the printed list is still the mess you started with.

In `clean_line`: strip first, return `None` for an empty result or one starting with `#`, then collapse runs of whitespace with `re.sub`. Split into at most three parts, return `None` if you got fewer, and rebuild with the level upper case and the rest lower case.
A two-step split is the useful one here: `"a b c d".split(" ", 2)` gives `["a", "b", "c d"]`, so the third piece keeps its own spaces.

import re


def clean_line(line):
    text = line.strip()
    if not text or text.startswith("#"):
        return None
    text = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", text)
    parts = text.split(" ", 2)
    if len(parts) < 3:
        return None
    stamp, level, rest = parts
    return f"{stamp} {level.upper()} {rest.lower()}"


def clean_log(lines):
    out = []
    for line in lines:
        cleaned = clean_line(line)
        if cleaned is not None:
            out.append(cleaned)
    return out


RAW = [
    "  2041-03-02   err   North Sensor COLD  ",
    "# maintenance note",
    "",
    "2041-03-02 warn East Damp",
]
print(clean_log(RAW))

description: Normalise the messy station log into lines you can compare.
